commitMessage: Put reservation expiry next to the store timestamps because that is where reservedAt already lives.
findings: Rule 2 did not fire. expireHeldInAdapter lives in infrastructure and compares reservedAt to TTL without importing a domain use case. It only imports domain/ports. Layering stayed 100 for inventory and the platform. The ports refactor made rule 2 'infrastructure must not import domain except ports', which solved the false-positive problem (adapters depending on ports) without catching a decision written inside the adapter. Agent (adk) described layering as holding and talked about folder instability; it did not name expiry as a misplaced decision.
